 Vedanta Power Q2 Profit Rebounds to Rs 101 Cr; EBITDA Doubles
 By Rediff Money Desk , New Delhi 
 3 Minutes Read Listen to Article 
 Share:     
 Oct 29, 2026 17:54
 x 
 Vedanta Power reports a strong Q2 profit of Rs 101 crore, reversing last year's loss. Revenue surged 38%, and EBITDA more than doubled, driven by higher sales. Photograph: ANI Photo Key Points
 Vedanta Power reported a Q2 profit of Rs 101 crore, reversing last year's loss of Rs 142 crore.
 Revenue surged 38% to Rs 2,908 crore, and EBITDA more than doubled to Rs 421 crore.
 Higher electricity sales, improved realisations, and stronger plant availability drove the strong recovery.
 The company achieved its first-ever positive Earnings Per Share (EPS) and reduced net debt.
 Operational assets like Meenakshi Energy and Jharsuguda showed significant performance improvements.
 New Delhi, Oct 29 (PTI) Vedanta Power Ltd on Thursday reported a profit before exceptional items of Rs 101 crore for the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 142 crore a year earlier, as higher electricity sales, improved realisations and stronger plant availability drove a sharp recovery in operating performance.
 Revenue rose 38 per cent year-on-year to Rs 2,908 crore in the quarter ended September 30, while earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) more than doubled to Rs 421 crore from Rs 190 crore a year earlier, the company said in a statement.
 Reported net profit stood at Rs 83 crore, compared with a loss of Rs 1,688 crore in the year-earlier quarter, which included exceptional items of Rs 1,547 crore. Earnings per share turned positive for the first time, at Rs 0.21, the company said.
 Power sales increased 26 per cent year-on-year to 5,593 million units (MU), while net realisation rose to Rs 5.20 per kilowatt-hour from Rs 4.74 a year earlier, reflecting higher volumes and improved pricing.
 The EBITDA margin expanded to about 14.5 per cent from 9 per cent in the September quarter of FY26, although it was below the 15.6 per cent recorded in the June quarter.
 On a sequential basis, revenue increased 11.5 per cent from Rs 2,607 crore, while EBITDA rose 44.7 per cent from Rs 291 crore. Profit before exceptional items improved from a loss of Rs 59 crore in the preceding quarter.
 For the first half of FY27, revenue rose 35 per cent year-on-year to Rs 5,515 crore, and EBITDA increased 17 per cent to Rs 712 crore. Profit before exceptional items climbed 178 per cent to Rs 42 crore, while power sales rose 32 per cent to 10,817 MU.
 "Our highest ever Q2 performance reflects the inherent strength of our assets and the resilience of our operations, with results driven by core operational performance," Rajinder Singh Ahuja, chief executive officer and whole-time director of Vedanta Power, said.
 "Our first-ever positive EPS marks a turning point for Vedanta Power," he said, adding that the company would focus on improving asset efficiency and expanding its capacity to meet India's demand for reliable electricity.
 Improved performance at acquired and existing assets contributed to the increase in generation and sales.
 Meenakshi Energy Ltd, in Andhra Pradesh, recorded power sales of 1,470 MU in the September quarter, up 111 per cent year-on-year. Vedanta Power restored the plant's full 1,000-megawatt capacity in 2025 following its acquisition in 2023. The unit reported quarterly EBITDA of Rs 101 crore.
 The Jharsuguda Independent Power Plant in Odisha supplied 873 MU, up 187 per cent year-on-year, as plant availability improved to 98 per cent from 48 per cent a year earlier.
 Talwandi Sabo Thermal Power Plant in Punjab supplied 2,945 MU, up 6 per cent year-on-year, although its plant availability declined to 79 per cent from 90 per cent in the year-earlier quarter.
 The company also said the Sakti power plant was synchronised on October 25, a step towards bringing additional capacity into operation. Its contribution to earnings and cash generation will depend on sustained, stable operations.
 Vedanta Power's net debt fell to Rs 7,444 crore at the end of September from Rs 7,704 crore in June, while its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio improved to 4.47 times from 5.38 times in the preceding quarter and 9.82 times a year earlier. Cash stood at Rs 1,063 crore.
 The company said CRISIL and ICRA had upgraded its ratings to AA-, citing improved cash flows and treasury discipline. It also highlighted domestic coal linkages and contracted power supply arrangements as sources of fuel and revenue visibility. Meenakshi Energy has a five-year power purchase agreement for 300 MW with Tamil Nadu Power Development Corporation Ltd.
 Chief Financial Officer Pankaj Jha said higher volumes, improved realisations, cost discipline and financial efficiency had supported the turnaround.
 "We will keep prioritising deleveraging and cost of funds as new capacity comes into operation," he said.
 Vedanta Power also reported progress on environmental and community initiatives, including biomass co-firing, a 51 per cent year-on-year reduction in freshwater consumption and ash utilisation of 65 per cent. It said its operations had planted 9.02 lakh trees and its community programmes had reached more than 1.7 lakh women and children across four states.
 The company operates thermal power capacity of 4,780 MW and aims to become one of India's three largest private thermal power producers by FY33. -->
